title: The Magnitude Mirage: Rethinking Confidence for Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval
abstract: arXiv:2609.15578v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many production RAG systems implement retrieval abstention by thresholding raw similarity scores, implicitly treating score magnitude as a confidence signal. We demonstrate that this practice degrades systematically as queries require reasoning beyond semantic matching. Across 11 retrieval architectures and 28 datasets, neural retrievers consistently assign high similarity scores to semantically related but constraint-violating documents, causing magnitude-based thresholds to collapse toward near-random abstention performance on logical and temporal reasoning tasks---a failure we term the Magnitude Mirage. To address this without computationally expensive alternatives, we conduct a large-scale empirical study of six zero-cost Query Performance Prediction (QPP) metrics across three cognitive tiers: semantic matching (BEIR), logical reasoning (BRIGHT), and temporal reasoning (TEMPO). tldr: 该论文揭示了“数值幻象”现象——相似度分数大小在推理密集型检索中会系统性失效，并大规模实证评估了六种零成本查询性能预测指标在语义匹配、逻辑推理和时间推理三个认知层级上的表现，以实现无需额外计算成本的可靠检索弃权。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals the "Magnitude Mirage" phenomenon—where similarity score magnitudes systematically fail as confidence signals for reasoning-intensive retrieval—and conducts a large-scale empirical study of six zero-cost Query Performance Prediction metrics across semantic matching, logical reasoning, and temporal reasoning tiers to achieve reliable retrieval abstention without additional computational cost.
